segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello. Welcome to another episode of Real Easy English, our podcast where we have real

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: conversations in easy English to help you learn. I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And I'm Georgie. You can watch this video with subtitles on our website,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: where you'll also find a worksheet to test what you've learnt. Visit

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hi Georgie, how are you?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I'm good, thank you. How are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm kind of tired today.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So you're tired. Well, today we are talking about naps.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Maybe you can have a little nap in the office later.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And a nap is when you have a short sleep in the daytime.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So, Neil, do you usually nap?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: No, I don't. I'm not very good at having naps.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I find it difficult to get to sleep in the day.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And if I do have a nap afterwards, I feel really bad.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah, me too.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: The only time I will ever have a nap is if I've got up really, really early.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: For example, if I've got up early for a flight, like 4am, then I might have a nap in the afternoon.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But I really avoid naps because like you when I wake up I feel worse I never feel better after a nap So I don understand people that nap all the time

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: My wife is an expert at napping

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Oh yeah

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: She can switch herself off

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and on like a light. I think it's an amazing skill. I'm very jealous.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah. Does she do it

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Often.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: She works very early and late sometimes shifts.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So I think if you have that kind of job, napping is really important.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I don't nap because it doesn't help me, but I really enjoy the actual process of napping.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It's nice to go to sleep, isn't it?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: You feel relaxed.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: You do, yeah.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I don't sleep enough, I don't think.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And it makes me feel good when I sleep well.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But usually I enjoy the evening so much that I don't want to go to bed early.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So you don't sleep very much or very well.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Does that make you tired during the day?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Often, yes, I feel tired.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But it's not as bad as it used to be because my kids are older now.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: How about you?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes I often feel quite energetic in the morning and then my energy crashes in the afternoon which is why I often drink coffee once in the morning and once in the afternoon to boost my energy

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Is there anything else you do to feel better, feel less tired?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Not at the moment, but I know that when I exercise, that helps me feel more energetic,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: which is strange because you think that would make you more tired,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: but it often gives people energy.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: What about you? Any tips for feeling less tired?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, I absolutely agree.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: If you're feeling tired, sometimes a good thing to do is do some exercise

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: or go and get some fresh air, go for a walk.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And instead of making you feel more tired, it makes you wake up a bit.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So I often feel very energetic in the morning, but then my energy crashes in the afternoon.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Do you have the same, Neil? Do you find your energy crashing or going down in the afternoon?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, sometimes. Sometimes in the afternoon, I yawn a lot.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: A yawn is when you open your mouth and breathe deeply.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'll show people. And you go...

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, I've seen you do that in the office, you yawn a lot.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah sorry I seen people actually in our office snoozing

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Having a snooze like having a little nap I seen it too

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah And not because they lazy because sometimes people here have to work very late at night or very early in the morning

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So they're tired.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've heard in this programme, starting with nap.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: A nap is a short sleep during the daytime.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And that's a noun, but it's also a verb to nap.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We also heard snooze, which is similar to nap.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: If you snooze, you sleep lightly for a short time.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we heard yawn.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: A yawn is when you breathe in deeply when you're tired like this.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I do it a lot.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We also heard crash.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: If your energy crashes, it falls or goes down.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: For example, my energy often crashes in the afternoon.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: but we'll be back next week with another real conversation in Easy English.

segments.text: And why not try our new easy video series, The London Letter Challenge.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: You can also find it on our website.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Goodbye for now.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Goodbye.
